court: Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación
crimes_charged: Crimes against humanity (aggravated homicide; criminal association — DINA agent, assassination of General Carlos Prats and Sofía Cuthbert, 1974)
summary: The CSJN held crimes against humanity imprescriptible on the basis of peremptory norms of customary international law incorporated with constitutional rank — decided against a Chilean DINA agent for the 1974 Buenos Aires assassination of General Prats.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Imprescriptibility of crimes against humanity under customary international law applies retroactively without violating legality.

case_name: José Efraín Ríos Montt & Mauricio Rodríguez Sánchez (Guatemala — Ixil genocide)
court: Tribunal Primero de Sentencia Penal de Mayor Riesgo A / Corte de Constitucionalidad
crimes_charged: Genocide; Crimes against the duties of humanity
outcome: Conviction (80 years) annulled by the Constitutional Court on 20 May 2013; retrial ongoing at Ríos Montt’s death (2018); Rodríguez Sánchez acquitted (2018)
summary: The first conviction of a former head of state for genocide by a national court in his own country: on 10 May 2013 Ríos Montt was sentenced to 80 years for the genocide of the Maya Ixil. Ten days later the Corte de Constitucionalidad annulled the verdict on procedural grounds. The CC’s amparo line around the trial is indexed on its official portal.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Head-of-state accountability before domestic courts; amparo as both a defence tool and a systemic obstacle; victims’ participation (querellantes adhesivos).

case_name: Alberto Fujimori (Peru — Barrios Altos / La Cantuta)
court: Sala Penal Especial de la Corte Suprema / Tribunal Constitucional
crimes_charged: Crimes against humanity (qualified homicide, grave injuries, aggravated kidnapping — Barrios Altos and La Cantuta)
outcome: 25 years imprisonment (2009); humanitarian pardon litigation 2017-2023; released Dec 2023; died Sept 2024
summary: The first conviction of a democratically elected former head of state, extradited by his own region, for crimes against humanity: 25 years for the Barrios Altos and La Cantuta killings under autoría mediata (control over an organised apparatus of power). The Tribunal Constitucional’s habeas corpus / pardon line (2022-2025) governed his release against the IACtHR’s objections.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Autoría mediata of a head of state over an organised apparatus of power; pardon vs. supranational obligations; victims’ rights in execution of sentence.

court: Supreme Court of the United States
crimes_charged: Arbitrary detention (cross-border abduction) — ATS civil claim
summary: The framework ruling limiting ATS claims to violations of international-law norms as specific, universal and obligatory as the 18th-century paradigms — the gateway through which every modern ATS atrocity claim must pass.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: ATS is jurisdictional; federal courts may recognise a narrow set of causes of action for specific, universal, obligatory norms of international law.

case_name: Yousuf v. Samantar (US — Somalia, foreign-official immunity)
court: Supreme Court of the United States / Fourth Circuit
crimes_charged: Torture; Extrajudicial killing (TVPA/ATS civil)
outcome: No immunity; $21 million judgment against Samantar (2012)
summary: Somali victims sued former Prime Minister and Defence Minister Mohamed Ali Samantar. The Supreme Court held the FSIA does not shield individual foreign officials; on remand the Fourth Circuit held there is no common-law immunity for jus cogens violations — one of the clearest national immunity rulings anywhere.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: FSIA inapplicable to individual officials; no foreign-official immunity for jus cogens violations (4th Cir. 2012).

case_name: Kadić v. Karadžić (US — Bosnia, private-actor liability)
court: U.S. Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
crimes_charged: Genocide; War crimes; Crimes against humanity (civil)
outcome: Claims reinstated; $4.5 billion default jury verdict (2000)
summary: Bosnian victims sued Radovan Karadžić in New York. The Second Circuit held that genocide and war crimes are actionable against private individuals without state action, and that a de facto authority’s leader can be reached — a pillar of civil accountability for non-state actors.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Genocide and war crimes do not require state action; ATS reaches leaders of unrecognised de facto regimes.

case_name: United States v. Belfast (Chuckie Taylor — first US torture-statute conviction)
court: U.S. Court of Appeals, Eleventh Circuit
crimes_charged: Torture; Conspiracy; Firearms offences
jurisdictional_basis: Active personality / extraterritorial torture statute (18 U.S.C. § 2340A)
summary: Roy Belfast Jr. (Charles “Chuckie” Taylor Jr.), son of the Liberian president, was convicted for torture committed as head of Liberia’s Anti-Terrorist Unit — the first (and long the only) conviction under the US extraterritorial torture statute.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Constitutionality and extraterritorial reach of 18 U.S.C. § 2340A; CAT implementation in US criminal law.

case_name: Forti v. Suarez-Mason (US — Argentine Dirty War, ATS)
crimes_charged: Torture; Prolonged arbitrary detention; Summary execution; Disappearance (civil)
outcome: Claims allowed to proceed; default judgment
summary: ATS suit by Argentine victims against General Carlos Guillermo Suárez-Mason, former commander of the First Army Corps — early post-Filártiga jurisprudence defining which norms are actionable, including recognition of causes of action for disappearance.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Actionability under the ATS of torture, prolonged arbitrary detention, summary execution and (on reconsideration) disappearance.

case_name: Xuncax v. Gramajo / Ortiz v. Gramajo (US — Guatemala)
crimes_charged: Torture; Summary execution; Disappearance; Arbitrary detention (civil)
summary: Default judgments against Guatemalan Defence Minister Héctor Gramajo in favour of Kanjobal Maya villagers and US nun Dianna Ortiz — command responsibility of a minister for atrocities by forces under his control.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Command responsibility under ATS/TVPA; service of process while the defendant studied in the US.

case_name: Doe v. Exxon Mobil (US — Aceh, corporate)
court: U.S. District Court, District of Columbia
crimes_charged: Torture; Arbitrary detention (civil, corporate defendant)
summary: Acehnese villagers sued ExxonMobil over abuses by Indonesian security forces guarding the Arun gas field. The 2005 opinion let core claims proceed; after twenty years of litigation the case settled on the eve of trial in 2023 — a pillar of the corporate-accountability strand.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Corporate exposure for security-force abuses; interplay of ATS, TVPA and state-law claims.

case_name: Sarei v. Rio Tinto (US — Bougainville, corporate)
court: U.S. Court of Appeals, Ninth Circuit (en banc)
crimes_charged: Genocide; War crimes (civil, corporate defendant)
outcome: Genocide/war-crimes claims reinstated en banc; dismissed after Kiobel (2013)
summary: Bougainville islanders sued Rio Tinto over the deaths surrounding the Panguna mine blockade. The en banc Ninth Circuit reinstated the genocide and war-crimes claims before the case fell to Kiobel’s presumption against extraterritoriality.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Corporate ATS liability for genocide/war crimes (pre-Kiobel); exhaustion of local remedies.

case_name: S v. Basson (South Africa — Project Coast)
crimes_charged: Apartheid-era murder conspiracy abroad; war-related crimes
outcome: Quashing of charges overturned; retrial ordered on the Namibia conspiracy counts
summary: The Constitutional Court rulings in the prosecution of Dr Wouter Basson, head of the apartheid regime’s chemical and biological weapons programme (Project Coast): South African courts had jurisdiction over the conspiracy to murder SWAPO detainees in Namibia, with the Court invoking South Africa’s international-law duties to prosecute.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Jurisdiction over cross-border conspiracy; international-law duties inform domestic prosecution of apartheid-era crimes.

court: Supreme Court of Israel (Court of Criminal Appeal)
crimes_charged: Nazi and Nazi Collaborators (Punishment) Law offences
summary: Leading appeal in Israel’s kapo trials: Hirsch Berenblat, commander of the Jewish police in the Będzin ghetto, saw his conviction under the Nazi and Nazi Collaborators (Punishment) Law overturned — the Court cautioning against judging the conduct of persecuted functionaries by ordinary standards.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Limits of collaborator liability; evidentiary caution in atrocity trials of persecuted intermediaries.

case_name: Public Committee Against Torture in Israel v. Government of Israel (targeted killings)
court: Supreme Court of Israel sitting as High Court of Justice
crimes_charged: Legality of targeted killings under IHL (judicial review)
outcome: Framework set: no blanket legality or illegality; case-by-case IHL constraints
summary: The targeted-killings judgment: a national supreme court defining the IHL rules — direct participation in hostilities, proportionality, investigation duties — that determine when a killing would amount to a war crime.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Civilians lose protection only for such time as they take direct part in hostilities; independent ex post investigation required.

case_name: Sentencia C-080/18 (Colombia — constitutional review of the JEP statute)
crimes_charged: Framework for war crimes and crimes against humanity of the armed conflict
outcome: Statutory law of the JEP upheld with conditions
summary: The constitutional review of the JEP’s statutory law: no amnesty for international crimes, conditionality of benefits, and the architecture of victims’ participation in the transitional jurisdiction. Bridges the corpus’s national layer and the tribunals layer (JEP).
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Amnesty limits for international crimes; victims’ rights as a constitutional axis of transitional justice; command responsibility standard.

court: Cour d’assises du Rhône / Cour de cassation
crimes_charged: Crimes against humanity (deportations, the Izieu children, persecution of resistants)
outcome: Life imprisonment (4 July 1987); pourvoi rejected 3 June 1988
summary: The first French crimes-against-humanity trial: Klaus Barbie, head of the Lyon Gestapo, brought from Bolivia in 1983, was convicted in 1987. The Cour de cassation’s 20 Dec 1985 arrêt defined crimes against humanity as inhumane acts and persecutions committed in the name of a State practising a policy of ideological hegemony — extending protection to resistance members.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Definition of crimes against humanity (20 Dec 1985); imprescriptibility; male captus (disguised extradition) no bar to trial.

case_name: Paul Touvier (France — Milice de Lyon, Rillieux-la-Pape)
court: Cour d’assises des Yvelines / Cour de cassation
crimes_charged: Complicity in crimes against humanity (execution of seven Jewish hostages at Rillieux-la-Pape, 29 June 1944)
outcome: Life imprisonment (20 April 1994); pourvoi rejected 1 June 1995
summary: The first final French conviction of a Frenchman for complicity in crimes against humanity: Paul Touvier, intelligence chief of the Lyon Milice, for the Rillieux-la-Pape executions.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Complicity in CAH of a Vichy militia official acting in concert with the Gestapo (state practising a policy of ideological hegemony).

court: Cour d’assises de la Gironde / Cour de cassation
crimes_charged: Complicity in crimes against humanity (arrests and internments preceding the deportation of Jews from Bordeaux, 1942-1944)
summary: Secretary-general of the Gironde prefecture under Vichy, later Paris police prefect and budget minister, Papon was convicted in 1998 for complicity in the deportation of Jews from Bordeaux — the trial of the French administration’s role in the Shoah.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Complicity in CAH does not require the accomplice’s adherence to the principal perpetrators’ ideology (Cass. crim. 23 Jan 1997).

crimes_charged: Accessory to murder in 300,000 cases (Auschwitz)
outcome: 4 years imprisonment; revision dismissed (BGH, 20 Sept 2016); died 2018 before serving
summary: SS bookkeeper at Auschwitz, convicted in 2015 as an accessory to murder for camp service during the Hungarian deportations. The BGH’s 2016 decision cemented the post-Demjanjuk doctrine: any function sustaining an extermination camp’s machinery grounds accessory liability.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Accessory to murder through service in an extermination camp (Leitsatz: “Beihilfe zum Mord durch Dienst im Konzentrationslager Auschwitz”).

crimes_charged: Accessory to murder in 170,000 cases
outcome: 5 years imprisonment; died 2017 before the revision was decided
summary: SS guard at Auschwitz I, convicted at 94 with numerous survivors as co-plaintiffs. The full judgment is published on the official NRW portal.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Camp-service accessory liability applied to guard duty (tateinheitliche Beihilfe zum Mord).

crimes_charged: Accessory to murder in over 10,000 cases (juvenile law)
outcome: 2-year suspended juvenile sentence; revision dismissed (BGH, 20 Aug 2024)
summary: Typist to the Stutthof commandant, tried under juvenile law (aged 18-19 at the time), convicted in 2022. The BGH’s 2024 judgment — the first extending camp-service accessory liability to a civilian employee — is probably the last NS-crimes ruling ever.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Accessory liability of a civilian camp employee; the closing chapter of German NS prosecutions.

court: Tribunale militare di Roma / Corte militare di appello / Corte Costituzionale
crimes_charged: War crimes (participation in the Ardeatine Caves massacre, 335 victims, 24 March 1944)
summary: Former SS captain extradited from Argentina in 1995 and finally sentenced to life for the Fosse Ardeatine massacre. The Corte Costituzionale ruled in 2000 on the 1953 amnesty raised in his proceedings — the constitutional layer of Italy’s late WWII prosecutions.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Imprescriptibility of war crimes; superior orders no defence; amnesty inapplicability.

case_name: Sentenza 238/2014 (Italy — state immunity vs. Nazi-era victims)
country_of_commission: Italy / Germany (WWII deportation and forced labour)
crimes_charged: War crimes and crimes against humanity (civil reparations claims)
outcome: ICJ immunity ruling denied effect in the Italian legal order
summary: The Constitutional Court refused to give effect to the ICJ’s Jurisdictional Immunities judgment insofar as it denies victims of Nazi-era international crimes access to a judge — the most consequential national ruling on immunity versus victims’ rights, keeping the Ferrini line of civil claims against Germany alive.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Access to court (Arts. 2 and 24 Const.) as a supreme constitutional principle overriding customary state immunity for international crimes.

court: Supreme Court of Canada / Federal Court
crimes_charged: Incitement to genocide, murder and hatred; crimes against humanity (immigration law)
outcome: Removal upheld; deported to Rwanda January 2012
summary: Léon Mugesera’s 1992 speech was held by the Supreme Court of Canada to constitute incitement to genocide and a crime against humanity for inadmissibility purposes — the leading national ruling on speech as an international crime outside the criminal process. The Federal Court line through his 2012 removal is on the official portal.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Speech as incitement to genocide and CAH; standard of “reasonable grounds to believe” in immigration proceedings.

case_name: Frans van Anraat (Netherlands — chemical precursors to Saddam’s Iraq)
country_of_commission: Iraq (Halabja and other Kurdish areas; Iran)
crimes_charged: Complicity in war crimes (supply of thiodiglycol for mustard gas); genocide complicity acquitted
summary: Dutch businessman who supplied thousands of tonnes of thiodiglycol used for Iraqi mustard gas deployed against Kurdish civilians, including at Halabja. Convicted of complicity in war crimes; acquitted of genocide complicity for lack of proven knowledge of genocidal intent. The leading business-accessory case for international crimes.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Accessory liability of a supplier for war crimes; knowledge standards distinguishing war-crimes from genocide complicity.

court: Kaunas Regional Court / Lietuvos Aukščiausiasis Teismas
crimes_charged: Genocide (participation in the 1956 capture of partisan leader Adolfas Ramanauskas-Vanagas)
outcome: 5 years imprisonment; conviction upheld by the Supreme Court plenary
summary: Former KGB officer convicted of genocide for his role in the capture of partisan leader Ramanauskas-Vanagas. The Supreme Court plenary held that the partisans and their supporters constituted a significant part of the Lithuanian national group — a holding the ECtHR upheld in Drėlingas v. Lithuania (2019).
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: National group “in part” may be defined through a politically salient subgroup (partisans); foreseeability of retroactive genocide liability.

case_name: Vytautas Vasiliauskas (Lithuania — genocide conviction quashed after Strasbourg)
crimes_charged: Genocide (1953 killing of two partisans as MGB operative) — conviction annulled
outcome: Conviction annulled and case discontinued (execution of the ECtHR Grand Chamber judgment)
summary: After the ECtHR Grand Chamber found an Article 7 violation (Vasiliauskas v. Lithuania, 2015 — the 1953 conviction was not foreseeable as genocide), the Lithuanian Supreme Court plenary annulled the conviction and discontinued the case — the nullum-crimen counterpoint to Drėlingas.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Legality limits of retroactive genocide prosecution; execution of ECtHR judgments in reopened criminal cases.

court: International Crimes Tribunal-1 / Supreme Court (Appellate Division)
crimes_charged: Genocide; Crimes against humanity (Rangpur)
outcome: Death sentence upheld on appeal (2019); reported acquittal on review, May 2025 — verify
summary: Jamaat-e-Islami leader convicted by the ICT-BD for 1971 atrocities in Rangpur; the Appellate Division dismissed his appeal in 2019 (official text in the Supreme Court bulletin). Reported acquitted on review in May 2025 after the change of government — a case now spanning both the accountability and reversal axes; verify the review judgment before relying on it.
additional_sources: Added from the 2026-07 Legal Data Hunter enrichment (see enrichment/ folder)
key_legal_findings: Appellate review of ICT-BD convictions; standards of proof for 1971 atrocity crimes.

crimes_charged: Torture (ordering, authorizing, inciting)
outcome: Defendant fled to Algeria; no proceedings
summary: TRIAL International filed a criminal complaint in 2009 while Soltani — a leader of the Movement for the Society of Peace and former Algerian minister — attended an event in Switzerland; he immediately returned to Algeria and faced no judicial consequences. The living-with-impunity archetype, complementing the Nezzar case.

case_name: 40 RPF officers & Rwandan officials (Spain — Judge Merelles indictment)
court: Juzgado Central de Instrucción No. 4, Audiencia Nacional
crimes_charged: Genocide; Crimes against humanity; War crimes; Terrorism (1990s killings of Spanish nationals and Rwandan/Congolese civilians)
outcome: Indictment of 40 officials (2008); dismissed by the Supreme Court after the 2014 UJ reform (Oct 2015)
summary: Judge Fernando Andreu Merelles indicted 40 RPF officers and Rwandan officials for post-1994 crimes, including the killings of Spanish missionaries and aid workers. President Kagame condemned the case; after the 2014 rollback of Spanish universal jurisdiction, the Supreme Court dismissed it in October 2015 — the leading example of UJ against a sitting regime and of statutory rollback under diplomatic pressure.
additional_sources: Referenced in Bryce/Johns/Langer, LJIL 2025 (doi:10.1017/S0922156524000244) and/or Langer & Eason, EJIL 2019 (doi:10.1093/ejil/chz050); details to be re-verified against primary sources.

crimes_charged: War crimes (Rwanda 1994 — Interahamwe financier)
outcome: 30 years imprisonment (1 Dec 2009); died in 2010 before the in-person retrial
summary: Banker and Interahamwe financier whose arrest was originally requested by the ICTR but who was tried in Belgium — convicted in absentia (illness) to 30 years in December 2009. Completes the Belgian Rwanda assize line.
additional_sources: Referenced in Bryce/Johns/Langer, LJIL 2025 (doi:10.1017/S0922156524000244) and/or Langer & Eason, EJIL 2019 (doi:10.1093/ejil/chz050); details to be re-verified against primary sources.

case_name: Milić Martinović (Kosovo — Sweden, acquittal on appeal)
crimes_charged: War crimes (Ćuška massacre, 14 May 1999)
outcome: Life imprisonment at trial (20 Jan 2012); acquitted on appeal (Svea hovrätt, 19 Dec 2012)
summary: Former Serbian police officer convicted at first instance to life imprisonment for the Ćuška massacre, then fully acquitted on appeal — one of only two universal-jurisdiction convictions reversed on appeal in the Langer dataset, and a key due-process data point.
additional_sources: Referenced in Bryce/Johns/Langer, LJIL 2025 (doi:10.1017/S0922156524000244) and/or Langer & Eason, EJIL 2019 (doi:10.1093/ejil/chz050); details to be re-verified against primary sources.

crimes_charged: War crimes; torture of Serb detainees (Dretelj camp, 1992)
summary: Guard at the Dretelj camp convicted of grave war crimes against Serb detainees — an investigation driven by Sweden’s national war-crimes unit, and the Swedish counterpart of Denmark’s Sarić case (same camp).
additional_sources: Referenced in Bryce/Johns/Langer, LJIL 2025 (doi:10.1017/S0922156524000244) and/or Langer & Eason, EJIL 2019 (doi:10.1093/ejil/chz050); details to be re-verified against primary sources.

crimes_charged: War crimes (outrages upon personal dignity documented in online postings)
summary: Two Iraqi nationals convicted in Finland in 2016 for war crimes documented in photos/videos they had posted online — with Sweden’s Droubi and Sakhanh, the founding examples of open-source-evidence prosecutions.
additional_sources: Referenced in Bryce/Johns/Langer, LJIL 2025 (doi:10.1017/S0922156524000244) and/or Langer & Eason, EJIL 2019 (doi:10.1093/ejil/chz050); details to be re-verified against primary sources.

case_name: John (Ivan) Demjanjuk (US extradition → Israel acquittal → Germany conviction)
court: US 6th Circuit / Supreme Court of Israel / Landgericht München II
crimes_charged: Nazi and Nazi Collaborators (Punishment) Law offences; accessory to murder in 27,900 cases (Sobibor)
jurisdictional_basis: Extradition + retroactive extraterritorial statute (Israel); surrogate territorial/personality jurisdiction (Germany)
outcome: Israel: death sentence reversed — acquitted (1993); Germany: 5 years (2011), died pending appeal
summary: The three-jurisdiction saga: extradited from the US (Demjanjuk v. Petrovsky, 776 F.2d 571 (6th Cir. 1985), endorsing universal jurisdiction for Nazi crimes), sentenced to death in Israel as “Ivan the Terrible” of Treblinka, acquitted on identity doubt by the Israeli Supreme Court in 1993, and finally convicted by LG München II in 2011 as a Sobibor guard — the judgment that founded the modern German camp-service accessory doctrine (Gröning, Hanning, Furchner).
additional_sources: Referenced in Bryce/Johns/Langer, LJIL 2025 (doi:10.1017/S0922156524000244) and/or Langer & Eason, EJIL 2019 (doi:10.1093/ejil/chz050); details to be re-verified against primary sources.
key_legal_findings: Wrongful-conviction prevention in atrocity trials (Israel 1993); the 2011 Munich doctrine of accessory liability through camp service.

case_name: Western Sahara complaints — Polisario Front / SADR officials (Spain, 2007)
crimes_charged: Genocide; Torture (complaints)
outcome: Complaint cluster (the 2007 spike in the Langer dataset); proceedings largely lapsed after the UJ reforms
summary: A 2007 campaign of complaints in Spain against members of the Polisario Front and SADR officials over alleged crimes in the Tindouf camps — the outlier spike of “living in fear” defendants in the Langer dataset, and a case study in autocracy-adjacent instrumentalisation of universal jurisdiction (Morocco context).
